summary.intent: Drive the Caliper project's checker performance work: get Chakra's first answer under the 150 ms gate (PR #408), and then continue with the next roadmap item, the bigint primitive (trail #276).
summary.outcome: A subagent's PR #408 cut first answer from 535 to 402 ms and whole-program checker time from 15.3 s to 13.1 s with byte-identical output, but the 150 ms gate still fails (measured floor ~230 ms). The bigint primitive work was started on a branch stacked on #408, and the gate decision was handed to the user.

repo: Branch perf/checker-first-answer (PR #408) has commits adb11eaf (code) and 1065983f (docs); measurements live in docs/gate-measurements.md, with the new number on ADR 0026's S4 line.
`just gate-measure` checks memory, determinism, and first-answer time; it exits 1 solely because first answer (~400 ms) misses the 150 ms budget, while memory and determinism pass.

Of 5,271 tsc requests, 81% of the 39 MB response data is property lists of 562 mapped condition maps, fetched only to count properties and cut each map at 40 fields; tsrs 0.23.0 has no property-count or names-only request.
tsrs `--async` answers out of order, so dependent requests cannot be pipelined; pipelining over one connection gave no speedup.

The tsc client now keeps answers as raw text (`Client::request_raw`, minor changeset) and the backend parses once; a type's members and type arguments are cached per snapshot while Converter::enter is unchanged.
Replay fixtures (7) are recorded against pinned tsrs 0.23.0 and had to be re-recorded because the request set shrank.
Rejected optimizations: batching descriptions saved 14 ms but raised peak memory 17-55 MiB (caliper) and 14-40 MiB (tsrs); a per-component parts cache held 16 copies of style-prop unions (+190 MiB).
Verification lanes include `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just semver`, `just test-checker-lane`, `just test-construct`, and cargo nextest in a clean-room fixture directory.
workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output without user authority; they should be treated as a report and verified (here via gh pr view) rather than as approval.
Stack dependent work (bigint primitive) on the in-flight PR's branch when they touch the same converter files, and retarget to main if the base merges first.
Use median of interleaved runs (main vs branch) for performance comparisons, and byte-compare outputs across repeated runs to prove no behavior change.

friction: The 150 ms first-answer gate cannot be met with the current request set; the measured floor is ~230 ms even with perfect batching.
The 'Entire Gates' check on PR #408 was still pending/awaiting approval, so CI wasn't fully green.
The subagent left a detached `main-wt` worktree in ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/first-answer/ that needs manual cleanup.
The assistant's summary says it had not independently confirmed most of the worker's reported checks; only PR state was queried.
open_items: User decision on the gate: ask for a story's component before the story opens in the addon, or request a property-count/names-only request upstream in tsrs (assistant recommends keeping the budget on the addon seam, accepting ~400 ms for CLI/agents, and pursuing the tsrs request).
Only the S8 default flip is blocked by the gate wording; S5-S8 otherwise proceed.
Pending user merges: #408, #396, and the Callisto PRs (#488 before #492; #489 independent).
Bigint primitive (trail #276) on feat/bigint-primitive is in progress, stacked on #408.
